subject: Conditional uptime floor for bursty workloads & proportional monthly credits
messages:
From: Evan Liu <evan.liu@cloudwave.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
Cc: CloudWave Procurement <procurement@cloudwave.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Conditional uptime floor for bursty inference workload

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — team was impressed with the latency numbers. A couple procurement items came up during our internal review.

CloudWave runs a heavily bursty inference profile: 80% of requests arrive in 1–2 hour peaks. Our concern is the template SLA language that measures uptime/loss against the month as a whole. During sustained peaks, short degradation can have outsized business impact.

We'd like to propose two items for the SLA template:
- a conditional uptime floor during sustained bursts (i.e., when 5-minute P95 request rate > X for Y minutes, uptime should be measured against a stricter baseline), and
- monthly service credits that are proportional to the severity during those burst windows rather than averaged across the month.

Attached is a CSV of our traffic profile. Can your team outline how Redwood would accommodate a conditional floor and a proportional credit calculation? If this needs legal review, please loop them in.

Best,
Evan
Procurement Manager | CloudWave

(attachment: CloudWave_traffic_profile.csv)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Liu <evan.liu@cloudwave.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Conditional uptime floor for bursty inference workload

Evan — thanks for sharing the profile, and great to hear the demo landed well.

Short answer: yes, we can support a conditional floor and a proportional credits model, but we need to align on precisely how "burst" is defined and on the math for credits to keep the remedy bounded and auditable.

High-level approach we recommend:
1) Define burst windows by a traffic threshold and a minimum duration (your CSV will help us pick X/Y).
2) During burst windows, measure availability against an elevated uptime baseline (e.g., 99.95% instead of the standard 99.9%).
3) If availability drops inside burst windows, calculate monthly credits proportionally to the time-weighted severity inside those windows, capped at a monthly maximum.

Ben — can you draft a proposed formula and cap we can share? Marissa, we'll need a quick review of legal implications (especially around the cap and reporting requirements).

Thanks,
Naomi
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>, Evan Liu <evan.liu@cloudwave.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Conditional uptime floor for bursty inference workload — proposed formula

Evan/Naomi — quick stab at a workable, auditable formula below. This is deliberately conservative on caps.

Proposal (draft):
- Burst definition: 5-minute request rate > 3x the monthly median 5-minute rate for at least 30 consecutive minutes.
- Elevated baseline inside bursts: 99.95% availability measured at 1-minute resolution.
- Severity calculation: For each minute inside a qualifying burst window, compute deficit = max(0, baseline - availability_minute). Aggregate total_deficit_minutes over the month.
- Credit = min(monthly_commitment * (total_deficit_minutes / minutes_in_month) * 1.5, monthly_credit_cap)
  - monthly_commitment = agreed spend for the month
  - monthly_credit_cap = 30% of monthly_commitment by default (negotiable)

Notes:
- The 1.5 multiplier reflects higher business impact of burst degradation; can be tuned.
- We'll produce the minute-level availability report and the burst window report as evidence.
- We can also offer an alternate where the cap is a fixed dollar amount instead of a percent.

Marissa — anything that legal would push back on in this structure? Evan — does the definition of burst look reasonable based on your CSV?

Thanks,
Ben
Head of Reliability Solutions | Redwood Inference

From: Evan Liu <evan.liu@cloudwave.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Conditional uptime floor for bursty inference workload — proposed formula

Ben/Naomi — thanks, this is helpful and closer to what we had in mind. A few comments from our side after a quick review:

- Burst threshold: 3x monthly median seems fine as a starting point, but can we make it explicit the comparator excludes short daily spikes (e.g., compute median over hourly medians)?
- Duration: 30 minutes OK; can you confirm how Redwood detects and stitches windows that have short drops between high-rate intervals?
- Cap: 30% of monthly_commitment is high for procurement; we'd prefer a sliding cap: 10% for standard months, 20% for months with >40% of traffic in bursts, and 30% only for sustained heavy burst months >60% burst traffic.

Also, procurement will want the credit payout process: automated invoicing vs. credit on next invoice, plus a 30-day window for dispute.

If you can provide a short redline we can send to our counsel, that would speed things up.

Best,
Evan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evan Liu <evan.liu@cloudwave.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Conditional uptime floor for bursty inference workload — legal view and redlines

Looping in a concise legal summary for Evan's team. Evan — attaching a redline (SLA_redlines_v2.pdf) that reflects:
- Burst window definitions with median computation language (exclude top 5% outliers for median calc)
- Stitching rule: gaps < 5 minutes join adjacent windows; separate otherwise
- Sliding cap as requested, with explicit triggers (percent of monthly traffic in burst windows)
- Credit remediation flow: credit applied to next invoice by default; customers may request payout, subject to a 30-day verification period and dispute window.

A couple of negotiation levers we keep: the multiplier (1.5) and whether certain maintenance events are excluded from burst calculations. We left those in the redline for clarity.

Evan — please review and let us know changes. Naomi — happy to join a short call with your legal if needed.

Marissa
Director, Commercial Legal | Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Liu <evan.liu@cloudwave.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Conditional uptime floor for bursty inference workload — next steps

2) Naomi/Ben/Marissa: finalize the minute-level reporting format and export (CSV + signed hash for audit).
3) Evan: share procurement counsel contact if they want to receive the redline directly (we'll prepare a short cover note).
4) Schedule a 30-minute sync Friday to close on the numbers.

If that works I will schedule the call. I'll attach the draft SLA redline in HubSpot for the record.

Best,
Naomi
